Isoloop 0.1.0 is the first release: event-loop isolation for JavaScript apps, as a complete toolchain.

- **Containment:** each part of your app runs as an isolate on an event loop of its own, or in a pool, where it shares one loop and fails with the others.
- **Restart and catch-up:** the supervisor restarts an isolate that blocks or crashes, and it reads what it needs back from the bus.
- **A bus:** typed topics with schemas, grants, retention and replay, and opt-in history that survives a reload.
- **Placement as a switch:** move an isolate between its own worker and a pool without changing its code.
- **Your UI:** React 18 and 19, Preact 10 and 11, plain DOM, or no UI at all.

## Install

```sh
npm install @isoloop/host @isoloop/runtime @isoloop/bus zod
npm install -D @isoloop/vite
```

Add `@isoloop/react` or `@isoloop/preact` for those frameworks. Any [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) library can take Zod's place. Then follow [Getting started](https://isoloop.dev/docs/getting-started/).

The command line needs Node 26 or later. It exports contracts as JSON Schema, runs a dev MCP server for coding agents, and installs the "build with Isoloop" skill:

```sh
npm install -D isoloop
npx isoloop skill add
```

## What's experimental

These may change or be removed in any minor version:

- **The balancer:** `@isoloop/balancer`, placement by measured load.
- **Agents:** tools on contracts, `agents.expose`, `kernel.request`, the dev MCP connection and `@isoloop/webmcp`. WebMCP is behind a flag in Chromium and Firefox.
- **Inspection:** `kernel.inspect()`, the `inspect` grant and `@isoloop/devtools`.
- **On the bus:** consumer groups, and request and reply.

On 0.x, a minor version may also break the host API and the kernel's config. A patch doesn't.

## What it costs

Isoloop costs CPU, memory and start-up time, and every isolate on a worker of its own adds to each.

On the 72-widget plant dashboard at 5 kHz, against native with workers, the `matched` placement used 53 percentage points less main-thread CPU and had 28 ms less typing latency. It used 19 points more CPU across all threads and 51 MB more memory, and showed its first data 294 ms later ([results](https://github.com/isoloop/web/blob/9b50967b0971871ec9671d7dce8d115eb16f6d19/apps/dashboards/plant/comparison/final/README.md): Chromium, a 4-core machine at 2.0 GHz, `0.0.0-next.b8ffdcf` as `plant-v0.1.0`, 2026-11-13). On an older iOS phone (Safari 16.6, the same date), the native build held 60 frames a second and Isoloop did worse the more workers it used ([what it costs](https://isoloop.dev/docs/limits/#what-it-costs)).

## Known limits

- **Not a security boundary.** Isolates share the page's origin. It contains failures, not hostile code.
- **No synchronous layout or page DOM.** Measuring, focus and scrolling are async calls, so libraries that need them at once don't work in an isolate.
- **Input is a message.** `preventDefault()` in an isolate comes too late, drag and drop isn't forwarded, and replies to input add latency.
- **No server-side rendering.** An isolate's content appears once its worker has started.
- **A looser style policy.** A page that shows an isolate's UI needs `'unsafe-inline'` in `style-src` ([hosting](https://isoloop.dev/docs/hosting/#content-security-policy)).
- **Browsers only:** Chrome 108, Firefox 114, Safari 16.4 or later.

All of them: [What Isoloop can't hide](https://isoloop.dev/docs/limits/).
